Chairman and CEO | products = [[Hotel]]s and [[resort]]s | services = * [[Resort management]] * [[Brand management]] * [[Tour operator]] * [[Travel agency]] * [[Destination management]] | revenue = {{increase}} {{US$|6.67 billion|link=yes}} (2023) | operating_income = {{decrease}} {{US$|305 million}} (2023) | net_income = {{decrease}} {{US$|220 million}} (2023) | assets = {{increase}} {{US$|12.8 billion}} (2023) | equity = {{decrease}} {{US$|3.56 billion}} (2023) | num_locations = 1,335 hotels; 322,141 rooms | num_locations_year = 2023 | num_employees = {{circa|206,000}} | num_employees_year = 2023 | subsidiaries = [[Apple Leisure Group]] | website = {{URL|hyatt.com}} | footnotes = {{Cite web|title=2023 Annual Report (Form 10-K)| url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1468174/000146817424000014/h-20231231.htm|publisher=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission|date=February 23, 2024|access-date=February 26, 2024}} }} '''Hyatt Hotels Corporation''', commonly known as '''Hyatt Hotels & Resorts''', is an American [[multinational corporation|multinational]] hospitality company headquartered in the [[150 North Riverside|Riverside Plaza]] area of [[Chicago]] that manages and franchises luxury and business [[hotel]]s, [[resort]]s, and vacation properties. Hyatt Hotels & Resorts is one of the businesses managed by the [[Pritzker family]]. Hyatt has more than 1350 hotels and all-inclusive properties in 69 countries, across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia. The Hyatt Corporation came into being upon purchase of the Hyatt House, at [[Los Angeles International Airport]], on September 27, 1957. In 1969, Hyatt began expanding internationally. Hyatt has expanded its footprint through a number of acquisitions, including the acquisition of [[AmeriSuites]] (later rebranded Hyatt Place) in 2004, [[Summerfield Suites]] (later rebranded Hyatt House) in 2005, Two Roads Hospitality in 2018, [[Apple Leisure Group]] in 2021, [[Sant Singh Chatwal|Dream Hotel Group]] in 2023 and [[Standard Hotels|Standard International]] in 2024.{{Cite web|url=https://about.hyatt.com/en/hyatthistory.html|title=Hyatt History|website=Hyatt About|language=en|access-date=2020-02-18|archive-date=2020-02-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215095952/https://about.hyatt.com/en/hyatthistory.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.businesstraveller.com/business-travel/2018/10/10/hyatt-to-acquire-two-roads-hospitality/|title=Hyatt to acquire Two Roads Hospitality|access-date=10 October 2018}}{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/standardinternational|title=Hyatt to Acquire Standard International and its Iconic Hotel Brands, The Standard and Bunkhouse Hotels, Expanding Its Leading Position in Lifestyle Hospitality}} == History == ===Foundation and early years=== The first Hyatt House was opened in 1954 by business partners Hyatt Robert von Dehn and [[Jack D. Crouch|Jack Dyer Crouch]] as a motel near [[Los Angeles International Airport]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.newspapers.com/newspage/118024752/|title=Arizona Republic from Phoenix, Arizona on July 31, 1973 · Page 5|website=Newspapers.com|date=July 31, 1973 }} In 1957, the hotel was purchased by entrepreneur [[Jay Pritzker]] for {{currency|2.2|USD}} [[million]]. His younger brother, [[Donald Pritzker]], also took on an important role in the company. Considering the growing use of air travel for business, the [[Pritzker family|Pritzker brothers]] realized that locating a high-quality hotel near a major airport was a valuable business strategy. Within two years, they opened Hyatt House Hotels near [[San Francisco International Airport]] and [[Seattle–Tacoma International Airport]].{{cite web|last=Tritsch |first=Shane |url=http://www.chicagomag.com/Chicago-Magazine/December-2002/Tremors-in-the-Empire/ |title=Tremors in the Empire - Chicago magazine - December 2002 - Chicago |publisher=Chicagomag.com |date=2007-06-21 |access-date=2012-10-30}} The company went public in 1962 as Hyatt Corporation. It had two divisions: Hyatt House Hotels and Hyatt Chalet Motels (renamed Hyatt Lodges in 1966).{{cite web | url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1468174/000119312513053397/d482917dex992.htm | title=Hyatt Investor Fact Book }} In 1967, the company opened the Regency Hyatt House in Atlanta, Georgia (today named the [[Hyatt Regency Atlanta]]). The futuristic hotel was designed by Atlanta architect [[John Portman]], who would go on to design many other hotels for the chain. It featured a massive indoor atrium, which soon became a distinctive feature of many Hyatt properties.{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlantamagazine.com/news-culture-articles/after-50-years-hyatt-regency-atlanta-is-still-a-visual-spectacle/|title=After 50 years, Hyatt Regency Atlanta is still a downtown icon|first=Thomas|last=Wheatley|date=July 10, 2017}} In 1968, Hyatt International was formed, to operate hotels outside the United States.{{Cite web |url=https://about.hyatt.com/en/hyatthistory.html |title=Hyatt History |access-date=2020-02-02 |archive-date=2020-02-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215095952/https://about.hyatt.com/en/hyatthistory.html |url-status=dead }} It would soon become a separate company. In 1969, Hyatt opened its first international hotel, when it was awarded the management contract for the President Hotel in Hong Kong, which was renamed the Hong Kong Hyatt Hotel (later known as the Hyatt Regency Hong Kong).{{cite web|url=https://industrialhistoryhk.org/the-kings-of-industrial-buildings-the-chung-brothers-of-e-wah-aik-san/|title=The Kings of Industrial Buildings - the Chung brothers of E.Wah Aik San|last=Lo|first=York|date=11 December 2017|website=The Industrial History of Hong Kong Group|access-date=2019-06-06}} In 1972, Hyatt formed Elsinore Corporation, a subsidiary to operate the [[Four Queens Hotel and Casino]] and the Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe Resort, Spa & Casino. Donald Pritzker died in 1972 and Jay Pritzker continued to run the company.{{cite web|url=http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/Hyatt-Corporation-Company-History.html |title=History of Hyatt Corporation |website=Funding Universe |access-date=2012-10-30}} Hyatt became a private company in 1979, when the Pritzkers bought the outstanding shares. Elsinore was [[Corporate spin-off|spun off]] as a public company. The company opened the [[Playboy Hotel and Casino]] as a joint venture with [[Playboy Enterprises]].{{cite web |title=Elsinore Corporation |url=http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/Elsinore-Corporation-Company-History.html |publisher=The Gale Group, Inc. |access-date=4 August 2009}}{{cite news |first=Arnold M. |last=Knightly |title=Gaming pioneer Jeanne Hood dies |url= http://www.lvrj.com/news/52422462.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007091759/http://www.lvrj.com/news/52422462.html|archive-date=2012-10-07|work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |date=2009-08-04 |access-date=4 August 2009}} Alongside the Hyatt Regency brand, the company introduced the Grand Hyatt brand in 1980, with the opening of the [[Hyatt Grand Central New York|Grand Hyatt New York]] (now Hyatt Grand Central). That same year, the boutique Park Hyatt brand was also introduced. The Pritzkers took Hyatt International private as well, in 1982. However, Hyatt and Hyatt International remained two separate companies until June 2004, when substantially all of the hospitality assets owned by the Pritzker family business interests, including Hyatt Corporation and Hyatt International Corporation, were consolidated under a single entity called Global Hyatt Corp. On June 30, 2009, Global Hyatt Corporation changed its name to Hyatt Hotels Corporation.Hyatt Hotels Corporation 2010 annual report, Part 1, Item 1, page 3 ===Development since the 2000s=== In December 2004, Hyatt Hotels Corporation acquired [[AmeriSuites]], an upscale chain of all-suite business class hotels from affiliates of the [[Blackstone Group]], a [[New York City|New York]]-based private equity investment firm. Blackstone had inherited AmeriSuites from its 2004 acquisition of Prime Hospitality.{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB110255436928295172 |title=About Hyatt |publisher=Hyatt.com |date=2004-12-09 |access-date=2019-07-05}} The AmeriSuites chain was rebranded and called Hyatt Place, a competitor to the limited-service products [[Marriott International]]'s Courtyard by Marriott and [[Hilton Worldwide]]'s [[Hilton Garden Inn]]. In December 2005, Hyatt acquired limited service company [[Summerfield Suites]] from the Blackstone Group. Blackstone had inherited Summerfield Suites from its purchase of [[Wyndham International]]. In January 2012, Hyatt Summerfield Suites were rebranded as Hyatt House in 2012 to compete in the "upscale extended stay market" against [[Residence Inn]], Homewood Suites, and Staybridge Suites.{{cite web |url=http://hyattpressroom.com/hyatt/en/news_releases0/2012/Hyatt-Officially-Welcomes-Hyatt-House-to-the-Neighborhood.html |title=Hyatt Officially Welcomes Hyatt House to the Neighborhood |publisher=Hyattpressroom.com |access-date=2012-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120903185453/http://hyattpressroom.com/hyatt/en/news_releases0/2012/Hyatt-Officially-Welcomes-Hyatt-House-to-the-Neighborhood.html |archive-date=2012-09-03 |url-status=dead }} Hyatt launched its first lifestyle brand, Andaz, in April 2007.{{Cite web|url=http://asia.news.yahoo.com/070413/4/308se.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070706052243/http://asia.news.yahoo.com/070413/4/308se.html|title=Hyatt Hotels Corporation Announces Andaz(TM)|archive-date=July 6, 2007}} Hindi for the word 'style', Andaz is positioned as a luxury brand, with the first hotel being a rebrand of the [[Great Eastern Hotel, London|Great Eastern Hotel]] in [[London]], followed by hotels in [[San Diego]], [[West Hollywood]], [[Shanghai]]{{cite web|url=http://shanghai.andaz.hyatt.com/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103040332/http://shanghai.andaz.hyatt.com/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 3, 2013|title=Boutique 5 Star Hotels in Shanghai, China丨Andaz Xintiandi, Shanghai丨Hyatt|work=hyatt.com}} and [[New York City]]. In August 2009, it was reported that Hyatt Hotels Corporation filed plans to raise up to $1.15 billion in an initial share sale. That November Hyatt completed an initial public offering and began trading publicly on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] under the symbol ''H.''{{cite web |url=http://hyattpressroom.com/hyatt/en/news_releases0/2009/Hyatt-Hotels-Corporation-Prices-Initial-Public-Offering.html |title=Hyatt Hotels Corporation Prices Initial Public Offering |publisher=Hyattpressroom.com |access-date=2012-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407065142/http://hyattpressroom.com/hyatt/en/news_releases0/2009/Hyatt-Hotels-Corporation-Prices-Initial-Public-Offering.html |archive-date=2014-04-07 |url-status=dead }} According to the filing [[Mark Hoplamazian|Mark S. Hoplamazian]] was to serve as [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] and [[Thomas Pritzker]] as [[Chairman|Executive Chairman]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=newsarchive&sid=an9vQvtdbo_E |publisher=BloombergLPcom |title=Hyatt to Raise Up to $1.15 Billion in Share Sale |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104073714/https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=newsarchive&sid=an9vQvtdbo_E |archive-date=2012-11-04 |author=Nadja Brandt |date=August 6, 2009}} The public offering was a result of the acrimonious breakup of the Pritzker family empire. Accused of looting family trusts, Thomas and cousins Penny and Nicholas took control of the family businesses when they and other family members were sued by cousin [[Liesel Pritzker]], claiming fraud and seeking damages of over [[US$]]6 billion.{{cite web|last=Andrews |first=Suzanna |url=http://www.vanityfair.com/fame/features/2003/05/andrews200305 |title=Shattered Dynasty |date=May 2003 |publisher=Vanity Fair |access-date=2012-10-30}} On August 31, 2009 three Hyatt hotels in Boston laid off their entire housekeeping staffs, outsourcing the work to a Georgia company creating strong public backlash.{{cite news |url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/hotelcheckin/post/2009/09/68499403/1|publisher=USA Today | title=Reader to Hyatt Hotels: "Shame on you" for outsourcing housekeepers | date=September 20, 2009}} Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] threatened a boycott of the hotels by state employees traveling on official business.{{cite news |url=http://www.boston.com/business/articles/2009/09/19/patrick_troubled_by_hyatt/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090926064056/http://www.boston.com/business/articles/2009/09/19/patrick_troubled_by_hyatt/ |archive-date=September 26, 2009 |publisher=Boston Globe|title=Patrick ‘troubled’ by Hyatt: Governor asks CEO to rethink cuts to housekeeping staff | date = September 19, 2009 }}Whitford, David, "[http://money.cnn.com/2009/09/30/news/companies/hyatt_hotels_boston.fortune/index.htm?postversion=2009093012 A mess: Hyatt's housekeeping scandal]", ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'', Sep 30, 2009. The housekeepers, who were fired without previous notice although some of them had worked for the Hyatt for over 20 years, became collectively known as [[the Hyatt 100]]. In December 2009, Hyatt was named the "Massachusetts Scrooge of the Year" by [[Jobs with Justice]]. On September 1, 2011, Hyatt acquired Hotel Sierra, which had 18 properties in 10 states. Along with Hyatt Summerfield Suites hotels, several of these properties were rebranded as Hyatt House in January 2012.{{cite web |url=http://www.hyatt.com/hyatt/hotelsierra/default.htm |title=Hotel Sierra Joins Hyatt |publisher=Hyatt.com |date=2011-09-01 |access-date=2012-10-30 |archive-date=September 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926135657/http://www.hyatt.com/hyatt/hotelsierra/default.htm |url-status=dead }} In November 2013, Hyatt introduced their first [[all-inclusive resort]] brands, Hyatt Ziva and Hyatt Zilara, with the first resorts being opened in Cancun, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos and Rose Hall, Montego Bay, Jamaica. On October 28, 2015, Hyatt announced that they were in advanced talks to acquire [[Starwood Hotels and Resorts|Starwood]] Hotels in a cash and stock transaction. The transaction was not completed, and Starwood was acquired by [[Marriott International]] instead.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-11-16/marriott-buying-starwood-in-deal-valued-at-12-2-billion|title=Marriott Buying Starwood in Deal Valued at $12.2 Billion|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319043214/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-11-16/marriott-buying-starwood-in-deal-valued-at-12-2-billion|archive-date=2016-03-19|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|date=16 November 2015 |access-date=2020-07-05}} In 2018, Hyatt saw expansion with the acquisition of Two Roads Hospitality. This added the [[Joie de Vivre Hospitality|Joie de Vivre]], [[Destination Hotels|Destination]], [[Alila Hotels and Resorts|Alila]], and Thompson hotel brands to the Hyatt portfolio, a growth of 85 hotels in 23 markets.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hyatt.com/info/two-roads-hospitality|title=Hyatt to acquire Two Roads Hospitality|website=www.hyatt.com|access-date=February 2, 2020|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021054717/https://www.hyatt.com/info/two-roads-hospitality|url-status=dead}} In March 2021, Hyatt announced the official opening of Hyatt's 1,000th hotel worldwide, Alila Napa Valley in St. Helena, California.{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=HospiBiz|title=Hyatt celebrates sustained growth with 1,000th global hotel opening - HOSPIBIZ|date=15 March 2021|url=https://hospibiz.com/hyatt-celebrates-sustained-growth-with-1000th-global-hotel-opening/|access-date=2021-03-20|language=en-US|archive-date=August 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824091854/https://hospibiz.com/hyatt-celebrates-sustained-growth-with-1000th-global-hotel-opening/|url-status=dead}} In August 2021, Hyatt acquired [[Apple Leisure Group]] (ALG), a luxury resort-management services, travel and hospitality group, from affiliates of [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts]] and KSL Capital Partners for $2.7 billion in cash. ALG's hotel portfolio consists of over 33,000 rooms operating in 10 countries. The acquisition will extend Hyatt's brand footprint into 11 more European markets.{{Cite web|url=https://investors.hyatt.com/investor-relations/our-company/default.aspx|title=Hyatt Hotels Corporation - Investor Relations - Our Company|website=investors.hyatt.com|access-date=July 20, 2020|archive-date=July 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711123705/https://investors.hyatt.com/investor-relations/our-company/default.aspx|url-status=dead}} In November 2022, Hyatt acquired [[Sant Singh Chatwal|Dream Hotels Group]], a lifestyle hotel operator for $125 million, with up to an additional $175 million over the next six years as properties come into the pipeline and open. Dream Hotels Group's portfolio include 12 managed or franchised lifestyle hotels under four brands.{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/news-releases?item=124315|title=Hyatt Continues Asset-Light Growth Strategy with Plans to Acquire Dream Hotel Group}} In April 2023, Hyatt acquired Mr and Mrs Smith, a UK-based platform offering direct booking access to over 1,500 boutique and luxury properties worldwide for £53.0 million in cash consideration.{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/news-releases?item=124323|title=Hyatt to Further Strengthen Position in Luxury with Plans to Acquire Mr & Mrs Smith}} In June 2024, Hyatt acquired the me and all hotels brand from Lindner Hotels AG, for which Hyatt has entered into a strategic collaboration with in 2022, consisting of six lifestyle hotels and over 1,000 rooms in central city locations across Germany.{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/Hyatt-acquires-the-me-and-all-hotels-brand|title=Hyatt Acquires the me and all hotels Brand, Positioning Conversion-Friendly Lifestyle Brand for Growth Across Europe and Beyond}} In August 2024, Hyatt announced the planned acquisition of [[Standard Hotels|Standard International]], an upscale boutique hotel operator, for $150 million, with up to an additional $185 million over time as additional properties enter the portfolio. The acquisition consists of 21 open hotels and more than 30 future properties under The Standard, Bunkhouse Hotels, Peri Hotels, The StandardX, and The Manner brands. With the transaction, Hyatt will form a new dedicated lifestyle group, managing all lifestyle brands and operations led by Standard International's Executive Chairman Amar Lalvani. Hyatt acquired Standard International in August 2024.{{cite news |title=Hyatt to Buy Standard International for up to $335 Million |work=Skift |date=20 August 2024 |url=https://www.skift.com/2024/08/20/hyatt-to-buy-lifestyle-hotel-group-standard-international-for-up-to-335-million/}}{{cite web |title=Hyatt Completes Acquisition of Standard International and Its Iconic Hotel Brands |work=Hyatt Newsroom |date=1 October 2024 |url=https://investors.hyatt.com/news/investor-news/news-details/2024/Hyatt-Completes-Acquisition-of-Standard-International-and-Its-Iconic-Hotel-Brands-The-Standard-and-Bunkhouse-Hotels/default.aspx}} That same month, Hyatt Regency Orlando, one of the region's largest convention hotels, was sold for $1.02 billion to Los Angeles-based Ares Management and Houston-based Rida Development — the nation's highest hotel sale in 2024.{{cite web |last=Kinbar |first=Sarah |title=Hyatt Regency Orlando sells for $1.02B to joint venture |website=Orlando Business Journal |date=2024-08-15 |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/orlando/news/2024/08/15/orlando-sees-largest-hotel-deal-of-2024.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-12-20}} The sale of the 1,641-room hotel at 9801 International Drive came to about $622,000 per guest room. In 2025, Hyatt closed on the sale of the real estate portfolio acquired from Playa Hotels & Resorts for $1.98 billion.{{Cite web |title=Hyatt closes on nearly $2 billion sale of Playa resort portfolio |url=https://www.travelweekly.com/Travel-News/Hotel-News/Hyatt-closes-on-sale-Playa-resort-portfolio |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=www.travelweekly.com |language=en}} ==Notable properties== [[File:Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme, 5 rue de la Paix, Paris 5 September 2011.jpg |thumb|Park Hyatt Paris - Aurora 2021-03-20.jpg|thumb|Hyatt House in [[Denver]]]] [[File:New York Bar Unplugged, Park Hyatt Tokyo (8376387540).jpg|alt=Bar of the Park Hyatt|thumb|Bar of the [[Park Hyatt Tokyo]] that featured in the 2003 film ''[[Lost in Translation (film)|Lost in Translation]]''{{cite web | url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/ericawertheimzohar/2023/09/07/park-hyatt-tokyo-20-years-after-lost-in-translation-this-iconic-property-looks-ahead-to-its-sequel/?sh=25c1f0701c2a | title=Park Hyatt Tokyo: 20 Years After Lost in Translation, This Iconic Property Looks Ahead to Its Sequel | website=[[Forbes]] }}{{cite web | url=https://www.uniqhotels.com/park-hyatt-tokyo/ | title=Park Hyatt Tokyo - the Hotel from 'Lost in Translation' Movie }}]] *[[Amman]], Jordan: On November 9, 2005, Grand Hyatt Amman was targeted by a [[2005 Amman bombings|series of coordinated terrorist attacks]] along with a Radisson SAS and a Days Inn hotel.{{Cite web|date=November 10, 2005|title=Hotel blasts kill dozens in Jordan|url=https://www.cnn.com/2005/WORLD/meast/11/09/jordan.blasts/|access-date=2020-09-09|website=www.cnn.com}} *[[Atlanta]], United States: The [[Hyatt Regency Atlanta]], the first Hyatt Regency hotel, was built in 1967 as the Regency Hyatt House, and was the first contemporary atrium hotel in the world. {{As of|2025}}, it was the only major downtown Atlanta hotel with a front drive on [[Peachtree Street]]. Architect [[John Portman]] designed the building. *[[Austin, Texas|Austin]], United States: [[Driskill Hotel|The Driskill]] is the oldest operating hotel in Austin, Texas, and a member of [[Historic Hotels of America]]. *[[Baguio]], Philippines: The [[Hyatt Terraces Baguio Hotel]] collapsed after a July 16, 1990, [[1990 Luzon earthquake|earthquake]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1041379|title=A story of unity, resilience: 28 years after the 1990 killer quake|website=PNA|access-date=2019-07-05}} *[[Bali]], Indonesia: Hyatt operates seven hotels on the Indonesian island of Bali: a Grand Hyatt, a Hyatt Regency, an Andaz, and four Alilas (Hyatt Hotels is a JV partner in P.T. Wynncor Bali, the company that owns the first three mentioned hotels). ** Hyatt Regency Bali, formerly Bali Hyatt, opened in 1973 as one of the first foreign-branded hotels on the island, and remains an important landmark in the [[Sanur, Bali|Sanur]] area. Following a five-year-long renovation, it was rebranded as a Hyatt Regency in 2018.{{cite web|title=A Quite Long History of Balinese Hotel Architecture Part I: Wija Waworuntu and Donald Friend|url=https://raditmahindro.medium.com/a-quite-long-history-of-balinese-hotel-architecture-part-iii-bali-after-donald-friend-9c81b2d42417|date=October 2, 2022|website=Medium|access-date=June 26, 2023}} ** Grand Hyatt Bali, opened in [[Nusa Dua]] resort complex in 1991 as the largest hotel in Bali at the time, featuring 630 rooms.{{cite web|title=A Quite Long History of Balinese Hotel Architecture Part IV: Massive Scale!|url=https://raditmahindro.medium.com/a-quite-long-history-of-balinese-hotel-architecture-part-iv-massive-scale-ef8acb965203|date=October 2, 2022|website=Medium|access-date=June 26, 2023}} *Bangkok, Thailand: The [[Grand Hyatt Erawan]] opened in 1991, replacing the government-owned [[Erawan Hotel]] at the [[Ratchaprasong Intersection]] in the modern-day city center. It is home to the [[Erawan Shrine]], which is popular among wish makers. *Beijing, China: The [[Grand Hyatt Beijing]] opened in 2001, followed by the [[Beijing Yintai Centre|Park Hyatt Beijing]] in 2008. *[[Birmingham]], United Kingdom: The [[Hyatt Regency Birmingham]] opened in 1990. *[[Burlingame, California|Burlingame]], United States: The Burlingame Hyatt House, the first Hyatt built by the Pritzkers, opened in 1959 near [[San Francisco International Airport]]; in 1988 it was demolished and replaced with the [[Hyatt Regency San Francisco Airport]]. *Cairo, Egypt: The [[Grand Nile Tower Hotel]] was operated as the Grand Hyatt Cairo from 2003 to 2011, when Hyatt pulled out of the country as a result of the [[2011 Egyptian revolution]] (though it ultimately returned to Egypt in 2021, with the opening of Hyatt Regency Cairo West{{cite web|title=Hyatt Centric to enter Africa with Cairo opening|url=https://tophotel.news/hyatt-centric-to-enter-africa-with-cairo-opening/|date=June 14, 2023|website=Medium|access-date=January 23, 2024}}). *[[Carlsbad, California|Carlsbad]], United States: The [[Park Hyatt Resort Aviara|Aviara]], opened in 2010, is a Forbes Five Star & AAA Five Diamond resort. *[[Casablanca]], Morocco: The [[Hyatt Regency Casablanca]], located in the Old Medina of Casablanca, joined Hyatt in the 1980s, having previously been operated as an independent hotel. *Chicago, United States: With 2,019 rooms, the [[Hyatt Regency Chicago]] is the seventh-largest hotel in the world, with the largest freestanding bar in the world. The hotel is known for views of the Chicago River and nearby attractions. *[[Dallas]], United States: The [[Hyatt Regency Dallas]], built in 1978, is most notable for its association with the Dallas landmark [[Reunion Tower]]. Originally freestanding, the base of the tower was integrated into the ground floor of the hotel after an expansion project in 1998. *Dubai, United Arab Emirates: ** The [[Hyatt Regency Dubai]], opened in 1980, is the first Hyatt property in the United Arab Emirates. ** The [[Grand Hyatt Dubai]] has 682 rooms, making it the largest hotel in Dubai at the time of its 2003 opening. *[[Dushanbe]], [[Tajikistan]]: The Hyatt Regency Dushanbe, opened in 2009, is Tajikistan's first Hyatt property, as well as the first hotel managed by a Western company following the [[dissolution of the Soviet Union]]. * Biarritz, France: Hôtel du Palais Biarritz – The Unbound Collection by Hyatt. The historic 19th-century seaside palace was chosen as the host venue for the 45th G7 Summit in August 2019, where world leaders including the US president and UK Prime Minister held bilateral meetings.{{cite web |url=https://clements.travel/travel-guide/hotel-du-palais-biarritz/ |title=Hôtel du Palais Biarritz: Inside France's Legendary Seaside Palace |publisher=Clements Travel |access-date=October 26, 2025}} *[[Ho Chi Minh City]], Vietnam: The Park Hyatt Saigon, which opened in 2005, is the first property of Hyatt in Vietnam. Located at [[Lam Sơn Square]], a plaza surrounding the [[Ho Chi Minh City Opera House|Saigon Opera House]] in [[District 1, Ho Chi Minh City|District 1]]. This site was previously home to the Brinks Hotel, which was used by the [[United States Army]] officers and was [[1964 Brinks Hotel bombing|bombed]] by the [[Viet Cong]] in 1964.{{Cite web |last=Bowyer |first=Mark |date=December 3, 2015 |title=Park Hyatt, Saigon |url=https://www.rustycompass.com/vietnam-travel-guide-233/ho-chi-minh-city-4/hotels-15/park-hyatt-saigon-243 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230402063644/https://www.rustycompass.com/vietnam-travel-guide-233/ho-chi-minh-city-4/hotels-15/park-hyatt-saigon-243 |archive-date=April 2, 2023 |access-date=October 22, 2023 |website=Rusty Compass}} *Hong Kong: The [[Grand Hyatt Hong Kong]] is the Asian flagship of Hyatt International. The [[Hyatt Regency Hong Kong, Sha Tin]] and [[The Masterpiece (Hong Kong)|Hyatt Regency Hong Kong]] are also five-star hotels in Hong Kong. *[[Jacksonville, Florida|Jacksonville]], United States: The [[Hyatt Regency Jacksonville]] opened in 2001 under the [[Adam's Mark]] brand. Ownership of the riverfront hotel changed along with the name in 2005. With 966 rooms, it is the largest hotel in [[North Florida]].{{cite web|title=Hyatt Regency Jacksonville Riverfront|url=https://www.emporis.com/buildings/118948/hyatt-regency-jacksonville-riverfront-jacksonville-fl-usa|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180506104048/https://www.emporis.com/buildings/118948/hyatt-regency-jacksonville-riverfront-jacksonville-fl-usa|url-status=usurped|archive-date=May 6, 2018|website=[[Emporis]]|publisher=Emporis|access-date=5 May 2018}} *Jakarta, Indonesia: ** Grand Hyatt Jakarta, opened in 1991, is adjacent to [[Plaza Indonesia]]. It is one of four hotels that surround the landmark [[Selamat Datang Monument]], alongside [[Hotel Indonesia|Hotel Indonesia Kempinski Jakarta]], [[Pullman Jakarta Indonesia Thamrin CBD|Pullman Jakarta Thamrin CBD]], and [[Mandarin Oriental, Jakarta]]. ** Park Hyatt Jakarta, opened in 2022, is touted as the first "six-star" hotel in Jakarta. It is located in [[Menteng]], a historically affluent district of the city.{{cite web|title=Opening Ceremony Park Hyatt Jakarta, Hary Tanoe : Park Hyatt Ke-46 di Dunia|url=https://nasional.okezone.com/read/2022/07/08/337/2626402/opening-ceremony-park-hyatt-jakarta-hary-tanoe-park-hyatt-ke-46-di-dunia|date=July 8, 2022|website=Oke News|access-date=June 26, 2023}} *[[Kansas City, Missouri|Kansas City]], United States: The [[Sheraton Kansas City Hotel at Crown Center|Hyatt Regency Kansas City]] was the site of [[Hyatt Regency walkway collapse|one of the worst hotel disasters]] in U.S. history. On July 17, 1981, two of the three skybridges that traversed the hotel's lobby [[Hyatt Regency walkway collapse|collapsed]] during a tea dance. The walkways were packed with people when a structural failure occurred, causing one bridge, which was hung from the bridge above it, to pull both bridges loose from the ceiling and collapse. The accident killed 114 people and injured over 200.{{Cite web|url=https://interestingengineering.com/understanding-hyatt-regency-walkway-collapse|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227121238/https://interestingengineering.com/understanding-hyatt-regency-walkway-collapse|archive-date=2019-02-27|title=Understanding the Tragic Hyatt Regency Walkway Collapse|website=Interesting Engineering|access-date=2019-07-05}} The hotel was later renamed the Hyatt Regency [[Crown Center]], and is currently operated by [[Sheraton Hotels and Resorts|Sheraton]].{{Cite web|url=https://timeline.com/hyatt-regency-skywalk-failure-8240bff34fa6|title=When this hotel skywalk collapsed, it was one of the deadliest structural failures in US history|website=Timeline|date=2 August 2017|access-date=2019-07-05 |last1=Buck |first1=Stephanie }} *[[Kochi]], India: [[Grand Hyatt Kochi]] opened in 2018 is the first Grand Hyatt Hotel in [[South India]].{{Cite web |last=archive |first=From our online |date=2019-05-04 |title=Grand Hyatt celebrates its first anniversary in Kochi |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/kochi/2019/May/03/grand-hyatt-celebrates-its-first-anniversary-in-kochi-1972340.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} *[[Kota Kinabalu]], Malaysia: Hyatt Regency Kinabalu, opened in 1979 was Hyatt's first hotel in Malaysia and the oldest international-branded hotel in the city.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} *London, United Kingdom: [[Andaz London Liverpool Street]], built in 1884. Formerly known as the Great Eastern Hotel, it was the only hotel in the [[City of London]] from 1884 until the 1980s.{{cite web | url = https://londonist.com/london/history/historic-hotels/ | title = Londonist| date = 15 December 2016}} *Los Angeles, United States: **Hollywood: The Continental Hyatt House (now [[Andaz West Hollywood]]) **[[Century Plaza Hotel]], operated by Hyatt from 2006 to 2016, was restored in 2021 as the Fairmont Century Plaza.{{cite news |last1=Leavy |first1=Jake |title=The 20 Most Anticipated Hotel Openings Of 2020 In The US |url=https://www.thetravel.com/most-anticipated-hotel-openings-2020-us/ |access-date=9 February 2020 |publisher=thetravel.com |date=30 January 2020}} *[[Maldives]]: Park Hyatt Maldives Hadahaa, located in [[Huvadhu Atoll]], has developed a reputation for being one of the most exorbitant and exclusive resorts in the country, on account of its remoteness from the capital [[Malé]] (a one and a half hour paid plane and speedboat transfers are required to reach the place). It was rebranded in 2011 from Alila Maldives, which had opened two years prior; in 2022, Alila opened another resort, Alila Kothaifaru Maldives, in the [[Northern Maalhosmadulu Atoll]].{{cite web|title=REVIEW – Park Hyatt Maldives|url=https://theluxurytraveller.com/2021/06/review-park-hyatt-maldives-deluxe-beach-villa/|date=June 4, 2021|website=The Luxury Traveller|access-date=June 26, 2023}} *Manila, Philippines: The Grand Hyatt Manila is located in the [[Metrobank Center]], the first [[supertall]] building in the Philippines (318m). *Mumbai, India: [[Grand Hyatt Hotel, Mumbai]] was designed by Chicago's Lohan Associates and opened in 2004. **In June 2021, the Hyatt Regency Mumbai closed, due to nonfunding for salary payment or operational expenses by Asian Hotels (West) Ltd., the owner of Hyatt Regency Mumbai.{{Cite web|title=Hyatt Regency Mumbai shuts down due to lack of funds {{!}} HOSPIBIZ|url=https://hospibiz.com/hyatt-regency-mumbai-shuts-down-due-to-lack-of-funds/|access-date=2021-06-09|website=hospibiz.com|date=8 June 2021|language=en-US}} *New Delhi, India: [[Hyatt Regency Delhi]] is a luxury hotel in New Delhi, India, built in 1983. *[[New Orleans]], United States: During [[Hurricane Katrina]] (August 23–31, 2005), the [[Hyatt Regency New Orleans]] received significant damage as almost all of its windows were blown out and the bottom floor was torn apart by [[flood]] damage. The hotel is located in the [[New Orleans Central Business District|Central Business District]] and reopened October 19, 2011.{{cite web|author=Jaquetta White, The Times-Picayune |url=http://www.nola.com/business/index.ssf/2011/05/hyatt_regency_reopening_in_oct.html |title=Hyatt Regency will reopen in October, 6 years after Hurricane Katrina |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521075736/http://www.nola.com/business/index.ssf/2011/05/hyatt_regency_reopening_in_oct.html |archive-date=2011-05-21|publisher=NOLA.com |date=May 18, 2011 |access-date=2012-10-30}} *New York City, United States: The Grand Hyatt New York, opened in 1980, was the first Grand Hyatt hotel and was the first major real estate development of [[Donald Trump]], in partnership with Hyatt. The partnership deteriorated into a tangle of lawsuits, and the Pritzkers bought off Trump's share in 1996. The structure, built in 1919, is currently named the [[Hyatt Grand Central New York]] and is set for demolition and replacement. *[[Oyama, Shizuoka|Oyama]], Japan: [[Fuji Motorsports Museum|Fuji Speedway Hotel]] (2022), on the premises of the [[Fuji Speedway]] motor racing circuit.{{Cite web |title=Fuji Speedway Hotel - Luxury Hotel by Fuji Speedway Circuit and Mount Fuji |url=https://www.hyatt.com/unbound-collection/en-US/fswub-fuji-speedway-hotel |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114080122/https://www.hyatt.com/unbound-collection/en-US/fswub-fuji-speedway-hotel |archive-date=2025-11-14 |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=www.hyatt.com |language=en-US}} *[[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], United States: On Mother's Day, May 9, 2021, a shooting at Hyatt Regency Phoenix left one person dead and seven injured.{{Cite web|url=https://www.azfamily.com/news/1-dead-7-others-hospitalized-after-shooting-at-hyatt-regency-hotel-in-downtown-phoenix/article_aabce6a0-b0be-11eb-b78b-6f0aee3ff51a.html|title = Survivor describes shooting at Hyatt Regency Hotel in downtown Phoenix that left 1 dead, 7 others hospitalized}} *San Francisco, United States: The [[Hyatt Regency San Francisco]] formerly housed a rooftop [[revolving restaurant]] called Equinox, offering 360-degree views of the city and the bay. The restaurant became a club for Hyatt loyalty members only and no longer rotates. The hotel was sold for close to $200 million to Dune Capital Management and DiNapoli Capital Partners in January 2007, about $250,000 per room.[http://sanfrancisco.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/stories/2007/01/08/daily3.html San Francisco Regency] – Sold *[[Seattle]], United States: [[Hyatt Regency Seattle]] is the largest hotel in the [[Pacific Northwest]], with 1,260 rooms.{{cite news |date=October 6, 2016 |title=1,260-room hotel in Hedreen complex will be Hyatt Regency |url=http://www.djc.com/news/co/12093668.html |work=[[Seattle Daily Journal of Commerce]] |access-date=October 18, 2016}} **[[Thompson Seattle]] opened in 2016.{{cite magazine |last=Russillo |first=Jack |date=2016-11-03 |title=Local Rooms: Thompson Seattle |url=https://www.seattlemet.com/travel-and-outdoors/2016/11/local-rooms-thompson |magazine=[[Seattle Metropolitan]] |accessdate=2025-06-23 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623090445/https://www.seattlemet.com/travel-and-outdoors/2016/11/local-rooms-thompson |archivedate=2025-06-23 }} *Singapore: [[Grand Hyatt Singapore]] opened in 1971 as the Hyatt Regency and with over 700 rooms, was also the company's largest hotel at the time. *[[St. Helena, California|St. Helena]], United States: [[Alila Hotels and Resorts|Alila]] Napa Valley was Hyatt's 1,000th hotel worldwide. *[[Taipei]], Taiwan: [[Grand Hyatt Taipei]] opened in 1990 as the "first international luxury hotel" in the country. *Tehran, Iran: The [[Parsian Azadi Hotel]] was opened as the Hyatt Crown Tehran in 1978, but Hyatt was forced to pull out after only a few months of operation, due to the [[Iranian Revolution]]. It was later reopened as an independent hotel. *Tokyo, Japan: The [[Park Hyatt Tokyo]] is the second-tallest building in [[Shinjuku]], Tokyo. It was the filming location of the 2003 film ''[[Lost in Translation (film)|Lost in Translation]]''. *[[Zanzibar]], Tanzania: Park Hyatt Zanzibar is the first Park Hyatt hotel in Africa. It is located in [[Stone Town]], a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and occupies a historic palace known as the Mambo Msiige.{{cite news |date=January 31, 2018 |title=Review: Park Hyatt Zanzibar (Tanzania) |url=https://theluxurytravelexpert.com/2018/01/31/review-park-hyatt-zanzibar/ |work=The Luxury Travel Expert |access-date=June 26, 2023}} ==Partnerships== In 2013, Hyatt partnered with [[MGM Resorts International]] in bringing 12 MGM properties in Las Vegas to Hyatt booking channels, as well as in-depth collaborations with each other's loyalty program.{{cite web| url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/2013-06-05-HYATT-AND-MGM-RESORTS-INTERNATIONAL-ANNOUNCE-NEW-LOYALTY-PROGRAM-RELATIONSHIP|title=Hyatt and MGM Resorts International Announce New Loyalty Program Relationship}} The partnership ended in 2023 when MGM partnered with Marriott International instead. In 2018, Hyatt began partnering with Small Luxury Hotels of the World, which allowed World of Hyatt members to earn and redeem points during their stays at participating SLH properties.{{cite web| url=https://www.hotelmanagement.net/operate/hyatt-hotels-partners-slh-to-expand-loyalty-program|website=Hotel Management |title=Hyatt Hotels partners with SLH to expand loyalty program |author= Rosenthal, Victoria | publisher=[[Questex]] |date=August 3, 2018 }} The partnership has since ceased in 2024 following Hyatt's acquisition of Mr & Mrs Smith, a direct booking platform of luxury hotels. In 2022, Hyatt entered into an exclusive collaboration agreement with Lindner Hotels AG, a German hotel operator, in bringing more than 30 hotels across seven European countries into Hyatt's portfolio under the [[Joie de Vivre Hotels|JdV by Hyatt]] brand.{{cite web| url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/news-releases?item=124298|title=Hyatt to Enter Exclusive Collaboration Agreement with Lindner Hotels AG, to Significantly Increase Brand Footprint in Germany and Key European Destinations}} In 2024, Hyatt purchased the Me And All Hotels brand from Lindner. == Loyalty program == Hyatt operates a [[loyalty program]] called '''World of Hyatt''', which replaced Gold Passport on March 1, 2017.{{cite web|url=https://newsroom.hyatt.com/102716Hyatt-to-Introduce-New-Global-Loyalty-Program-World-of-Hyatt|website=Hyatt.com|date=October 27, 2016|location=Chicago|title=HYATT TO INTRODUCE NEW GLOBAL LOYALTY PROGRAM "WORLD OF HYATT"|author= Royal, Russin}} This program includes membership tiers of base members, Discoverists, Explorists, and Globalists. The program offers Hyatt members benefits such as room upgrades and complimentary breakfast, based on how many nights they stayed in Hyatt-affiliated hotels or how much they spend in Hyatt properties.{{Cite web |title=An Introduction to World of Hyatt |url=https://www.chatflights.com/blog-posts/world-of-hyatt |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=www.chatflights.com}}{{Cite web |last=Steinke Hyatt Hotels Corporation, commonly known as Hyatt Hotels & Resorts, is an American multinational hospitality company headquartered in the Riverside Plaza area of Chicago that manages and franchises luxury and business hotels, resorts, and vacation properties. Hyatt Hotels & Resorts is one of the businesses managed by the Pritzker family. Hyatt has more than 1350 hotels and all-inclusive properties in 69 countries, across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia.
The Hyatt Corporation came into being upon purchase of the Hyatt House, at Los Angeles International Airport, on September 27, 1957. In 1969, Hyatt began expanding internationally.
Hyatt has expanded its footprint through a number of acquisitions, including the acquisition of AmeriSuites (later rebranded Hyatt Place) in 2004, Summerfield Suites (later rebranded Hyatt House) in 2005, Two Roads Hospitality in 2018, Apple Leisure Group in 2021, Dream Hotel Group in 2023 and Standard International in 2024.
